newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan 41-day NCDs average yield at 5.018 pct.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan 41-day NCDs average yield at 5.018 pct.

text.p: Taiwan's central bank issued T$12 billion in 41-day negotiable certificates of deposit on Tuesday at an average yield of 5.018 percent, a central bank official said.
The range of the bids was between 4.90 and 5.20 percent, the official said.
Central bank vice-governor Liang Cheng-chin said on Monday the bank was determined to keep short-term interest rates above 5.00 percent, but did not announce any specific measures.
The bank has been acting persistently to keep rates stable.
It issued T$8 billion in three-month NCDs on Monday to soak up excess liquidity in the money market, the latest in a series of such short-term paper issues.

Taiwan's interbank rate, which finished at 4.958 percent on Monday against Saturday's 5.008 finish, climbed back above the five percent mark at mid-session on Tuesday after the bank announced plans for the T$12 billion NCD issue.
Thirty-day commercial paper was at 4.95-5.00 percent at midday against 5.00 at Monday's close.
In October and November, Taiwan's overnight and short-term commercial paper rates were persistently below five percent, dipping at times below 4.5 percent.

The central bank responded by setting five percent as a benchmark target and issuing short-term debt from time to time, but has not taken stronger measures such as reversing recent decreases in the rediscount rate or reserve requirements.
